resources.string: Test sensorless starts and find the observer and open-loop settings that start the motor best

Starts the motor again and again and measures each start: how fast it gets up to speed, whether the observer keeps track of the rotor, how often the firmware falls back to open loop, backward twitches, current peaks. One setting at a time is changed between starts, in RAM only. Nothing is stored unless you apply the result.

Data used: a script on the controller samples the speed estimates, dq currents and voltages, observer and FOC angles and the flux linkage and resistance estimates every few ms. Alongside it come the realtime values, the streamed observer angle, the phase currents at switching rate for one start of each candidate, the firmware\'s resistance measurement and, after a fault, its fault log.
The script that measures the starts uses LispBM functions added in 6.05. Update the firmware first.
This tunes the sensorless FOC start. Run the FOC setup or set Motor Type to FOC.
The motor starts on its sensors
Sensor mode isn\'t sensorless, so the observer and open-loop settings don\'t decide how it starts. Hall sensors and encoders take over at low speed.
Resistance, inductance and flux linkage are needed to judge the starts. Run FOC detection first.
Clear the fault (it clears once its cause is gone) and try again.
Every start has to begin at standstill. Wait until the motor has stopped.
The battery is near its cutoff
The run would stop at the battery cutoff. Charge first.
The controller or motor is hot
The run stops 5 °C below the temperature limits. Let it cool down first.
LispBM didn\'t take the script or the script didn\'t answer. Check that LispBM works (Scripting) and try again.
The script reads different values than the config
Nothing was changed. Read the motor config again and retry; if it persists, report it with your firmware version.
Stopped: the kill switch is active
Stopped: the motor doesn\'t come to rest
Stopped: the measuring script stopped answering
The starting values are back on the controller. What was measured so far is below.

The script didn\'t answer, so the motor config as read before the test was written back. That also stored it, including changes that were only in RAM before the test. What was measured so far is below.
The starting values couldn\'t be set back. Reboot the controller to restore them; the test only changed them in RAM. What was measured so far is below.
The starting values couldn\'t be set back. Reboot the controller to restore them; the test only changed them in RAM.
The measuring script lost the app for a moment and set the starting values back by itself.
The script didn\'t answer at the end, so the motor config as read before the test was written back. That also stored it, including changes that were only in RAM before the test.
Thorough: observer type and open-loop timing too
Each setting is started at half, once and one and a half times the start current, so the result has to work across the throttle a rider uses, not at one current.
Every start runs forward. Use this where the drivetrain shouldn\'t turn backwards or freewheels in reverse (geared hubs), where reverse starts test a different load.
Record phase currents (slow over Bluetooth LE, off there by default)

plurals.name: tune_better_body
plurals.item: Median score %1$s with these settings against %2$s with the starting ones, better in %3$d of %4$d interleaved pair (lower is better).
Median score %1$s with these settings against %2$s with the starting ones, better in %3$d of %4$d interleaved pairs (lower is better).

resources.string: Nothing beat the starting settings by 10 % in median score and in most of the interleaved pairs without failing more often, so they are the best this test found.

Score: about 1 for a start like the starting settings\' typical one, more for slower starts, open-loop restarts, speed lost at the handover, backward twitches, speed ripple, observer angle error and current peaks; 10 and more for starts that didn\'t make it.
Writes the changed settings to the motor config. The rest of the config stays as it is.
In use until the next reboot. Ride it, then apply or reboot to go back.
Measured resistance differs from the config
The firmware measured %1$s mΩ, the config has %2$s mΩ. The low-speed observer depends most on the resistance.
Measured at %1$s °C; that is %2$s mΩ at %3$s °C, which is what was compared.
Without a motor temperature sensor the winding temperature is unknown and a warm motor reads high, so only a large difference is reported.
Without phase filters on this hardware the measurement is rough, so the test didn\'t try it.
Flux linkage while running differs from the config
Running starts showed %1$s mWb, the config has %2$s mWb. Run FOC detection again if this persists.
Some starts ended in a fault
The duty cycle neared its limit
It reached %1$d %% before the target speed, so the target is too high for this voltage. Lower it.
The observer loses the motor after open loop
With the starting settings the firmware had to start open loop again %1$s times per start on average.
With the starting settings the motor turned backwards at up to %1$s ERPM before it went forward.
The rotor falls behind the open-loop ramp
During open loop the rotor ran at %1$d %% of the open-loop speed. A longer ramp or a lower open-loop speed helps.
Phase currents reached %1$s times the start current.
